parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct, no documented border, facility, custody or police targeting of trans visitors, and hate-crime plus anti-discrimination protections in goods/services and health care since 2010-13. Against this, enforcement is documented as slow and uneven, the 2016 constitutional removal signals official ambivalence, and social attitudes are broadly disapproving of public LGBT expression. Ten logged bias-violence cases are a raw count with no background rate and cannot be assessed as a rate. No universal-exposure measure is documented; the main risk if outed is discrimination, friction and delayed recourse, not imprisonment.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border, passport-marker or ID-check friction for trans visitors is documented.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of gender expression; anti-discrimination law covers goods and services from 2010.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; absence of a documented domestic recognition procedure is not a visitor exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrest, detention, prison-placement or verification-exam practice for trans visitors is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific criminal offence documented; dissemination-of-homophobic-information offence targets hostility, not visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, shelter or other facility-exclusion rule is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers goods and services, education, housing and health care.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National law is the documented regime; no subnational variation is documented.

care_services.exposure: Social disapproval documented, including only 9.3% in 2022 accepting an LGBT family doctor; trans-specific care denial not documented.
care_services.protection: Health care explicitly covered by anti-discrimination law, expanded in 2020 to sex characteristics.
care_services.interaction: Formal coverage coexists with uneven enforcement and hostile attitudes, so access may be uneven in practice.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2016 removal of SO/GI from Constitution Article 18 under faith-leader pressure; opposition politicians in 2021 attacked LGBT school work as revolting.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2013 hate-crime amendment equates SO/GI bias with race, religion and disability; anti-discrimination commissioner issued reprimands and a favourable ruling.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective law and hostile political framing coexist; enforcement documented as slow and uneven.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No traveller-facing minor-specific rule, school-access restriction or family-recognition exposure is documented; no same-sex marriage or civil unions recognised.
minors_guardians.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers education; 2016 national school anti-bullying plan adopted.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's exposure would arise through general service and education attitudes, not a documented age-specific rule.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented as an assessable rate. A community log recorded ten bias-motivated cases against trans people in one year, with no general homicide rate for comparison.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime law since 2013 provides a legal basis for prosecution; commissioner ruled in favour in one mediated film complaint.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The ten-case count is raw and undenominated; it is not used as a prevalence or severity measure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are slow: only one of nine LGBT-linked cases concluded by Dec 2012; a deputy commissioner's reprimand came nine months after his remarks.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anti-discrimination commissioner can reprimand and rule in favour; UN expert visit in 2024 with report in 2025 made recommendations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protections exist but the record shows recourse is not timely or reliably effective, which limits their mitigating weight.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower risk / higher score than 0.35-B: that anchor has routine police stops, confiscations and fines for trans visitors. Here no traveller-facing police targeting, detention or extortion is documented, and no imprisonment pathway exists.

Similar to 0.65-B: formal care/service protections exist and a complaint mechanism can succeed, but implementation is uneven, socially resisted and slow. Here remedies are documented as weaker and slower than in 0.65-B, so a score at or slightly below that anchor is appropriate.

Higher risk / lower score than 0.75-A: that anchor has a health charter, an ombuds office that can order reimbursement and retraining, and only moderate delay. Here enforcement is documented as bureaucratically impeded, trust was lost, and broader social disapproval and constitutional removal are documented.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a protective statute set without a traveller-facing hostile rule: no criminalisation, no facility, border or custody exposure, and hate-crime coverage. The operative weakness is interaction, not a ban - social disapproval of public expression, hostile political interventions, and slow, uneven enforcement reduce the practical value of protections. If outed, the likely consequences are discrimination, friction and delayed redress rather than arrest or imprisonment. Uncertainties include document handling, facilities, custody, care practice and the true violence rate, none of which should be treated as safety.
